summary: This component renders a blog post with different layouts depending on whether you're viewing the full post page or a card in a list. It uses Docusaurus hooks to detect which view you're in, then conditionally shows post-specific features like related posts, reactions, and social sharing only on the full post page, while always showing the core post content, header, and footer.

explanations.23: This helper function checks if we're on the actual post page versus a list view, and returns a CSS class name for spacing only when it's a list view card.
explanations.29: The useBlogPost hook gives us metadata about the current blog post and a flag telling us whether we're viewing the full post page or just a preview card.
explanations.30: We're extracting frontMatter from the metadata object—that's the YAML or configuration data at the top of the markdown file that contains things like the author, date, and custom fields.
explanations.34: The article actions (like share buttons or edit links) only make sense when someone is reading the full post, not when they're browsing a card in the blog list.
explanations.46: This translation notice banner only displays on the full post page; it warns readers if the content has been translated and may not be the original.
explanations.55: This checks if the frontMatter has a tried_it field, and only shows the TriedIt component if that field is not explicitly set to false—allowing posts to opt out of this feature.
